label: False positives
summary: False positives in this context are similarity pairs that score above a threshold but don't represent genuinely useful or surprising connections. They are a core problem when using cosine similarity to generate link candidates in a knowledge graph: a threshold set too low floods the results with obvious or meaningless matches, burying the connections that are actually worth surfacing.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike frames false positives as a practical obstacle to making a link-suggestion pipeline actually usable. The 2,771 candidate pairs at a 0.55 threshold are the concrete example: that volume is too large to review, and the interesting cross-collection connections are drowned out by same-topic noise. She evaluates several filtering strategies specifically by how well they reduce false positives without sacrificing the rare surprising matches, with token blocking called out as a direct counter-measure because it avoids computing similarity for pairs that share no cheap signal at all.
open_questions: Whether per-document z-score normalisation can recover cross-collection pairs that a global threshold misses without re-introducing a different class of false positives.

Whether spectral thresholding, which requires no labelled data, would converge on a different cutoff than the manual threshold experiments, and whether that cutoff would reduce false positives more reliably.
